Trafficked Part 2

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We join police on a pre-dawn raid of a mysterious plot on the outskirts of Pretoria - the suspected hideout of a criminal gang dealing in forged passports, stolen cars and illegal scrap metal

Unique Selling Point:
We have been given an exclusive opportunity to join the SAPS National Joint Operations Command on the pre dawn raid. The sight is the suspected manufacturing facility for forged travel documents like SA Id's and passports. Also home to suspected criminals such as carjackers and illegal copper dealers. Also on site, about 70 undocumented foreign nationals from countries like Malawi and Zimbabwe. The SAPS team is apparently going to be quite a force - more than a hundred members including Tactical Response and the National Intervention Unit. Depending on what happens at the property and what is found, the SAPS are planning on making further arrests at multiple locations.

Summary:
This could possibly stand as a stand alone story or part of a bigger follow up story to our Trafficked piece.

Script:


Trafficked part 2
First Draft Script
22 April 2024

Intro
Upsound
Police Cars drive by

Voice
A pre-dawn meeting at the NatJoc - the National Joint Operational Centre in Pretoria. It includes officials from Home Affairs, several police units, private security and members of a counter trafficking NGO. 

Link Macfarlane
So it’s four o clock in the morning, we’re at the NATJOC, we’re joining the police on a raid.

Upsound Mac putting bulletproof vest on
Let’s rock and roll.

Voice
In March this year we lifted the lid on the large scale smuggling and trafficking of people across our borders from countries like Zimbabwe and Malawi.

We uncovered a sinister world - children hidden on buses and brought across our borders illegally, the exploitation of thousands of undocumented Malawians and the shady characters making money off it all - the transporters.

Upsound Hiddencam
Woman: Okay, we can negotiate. You can pay R5500.
Agent: R5500.


ACT 1

Voice
One way of crossing our borders illegally, would be to use a forged passport. And that’s what today’s raid is all about. The police are after this man, Ezara Chonchobe.
He’s a Malawian national, and a suspected member of a syndicate manufacturing forged travel documents.

Catching him red handed could break their case wide open.

Link Mac
So we’ve just left NatJoc and we’re going to raid this farm. Hopefully we don’t only find suspects, but also find all the evidence to prove what they’ve been up to on this plot of land.

Voice
It’s an intelligence driven operation – an informant has told police about a  smallholding in Grootfontein on the outskirts of Pretoria. 
 
Undercover surveillance reveals several buildings on the plot, as well as a large number of suspected undocumented foreign nationals. 

We enter the property as a drone fitted with thermal cameras monitors from the air. 
 
The size of the land and number of buildings present an operational nightmare.  There are many places for suspects to hide.  

Upsound police
On the ground! On the ground! Lala Panzi baba!

Voice
The police hit all the buildings simultaneously. They have a search and seizure warrant and are determined to catch the main suspect, Chonchobe, off guard.  

Upsound police kicking door
Get down, get down! Down, down, on your knees!

Voice
The house and surrounding buildings are filled with foreign nationals, as the informant said they would be. 

Upsound
Policeman: Where are you from?

Man: Malawi

Policeman: Malawi? Where is your passport?

Voice
Amid the chaos, the drone shows some suspects slipping away. The ground teams aren’t able to respond in time. 

Upsound search


Voice
As the search for Chonchobe continues, everyone found on the site is being questioned...  
 
Some, though, are refusing to hand themselves over. 
 
Upsound
Police at window as another door is being kicked

Voice
We join a search happening in a nearby maize field, and our producer catches the scene on his cell phone. 

Sound Up Mac
So we’ve got a drone up overhead, and it looks like somebody’s hiding here in these little cornfields. So we’re just going to go with police quickly and see if we can spot him.

Voice
Tension grows as authorities are unsure if the man is armed. 
 
But there’s no hiding from the drone, and he’s eventually nabbed without a fight. 
 
But that’s not the end of the drama. 

Upsound Macfarlane
There’s someone in the house there.

Voice
Moments earlier, a man fled from the house we’re now approaching. Law enforcement gives chase, but the suspect is too quick. 
 
He’s spotted crossing a nearby field where he has an unexpected encounter with an ostrich. 
 
When the drone is recalled for a change of batteries, he makes his escape. 

Upsound Mac
The suspect has ran through the woods here, but the police have gone to go chase him. We can’t keep up with the guys, they are much fitter than we are. But we can hear dogs barking everywhere, so hopefully they give chase and catch him. Let’s go see whats happening at the house.



Voice
Another man has been detained outside the house, while a woman has been locked inside. 

Upsound Police
Go open up the door. Police.

Upsound at door and kick door
Police: Where’s the key?
Man: How come you are locked inside?
Woman: Ja, it’s my boyfriend. Can you break it?
Man: Yes
Police: Yes, we break it. Thank you.

Voice
Like almost everyone here, the woman is apparently in the country illegally. 

Upsound Search
Emma: So why does he lock you up, did he just lock you up now?
Woman: Maybe he just see police, and just lock the door, and run away.
Emma: And he locks you up here?
Woman: Mmm.
Emma: Stupid boy.
Policeman: I suspect you are illegally here nê? You are illegally here, it expired.

Voice
By daybreak, the police have searched most of the property, and scores of foreigners are detained for being in the country without the correct paperwork.

Emma van der Walt and her team from the counter trafficking organisation Brave to Love are helping police to identify possible human trafficking cases.

Upsound Emma
Interviewing many of these people, yes people you know say they are in poverty in other African countries. But South Africa also has poverty. We have local people, good South African people, who are also in poverty. So now the problem is South Africa cannot be the breadbasket for Africa.

Upsound Teamleader
Teamleader: We’ve got about 20, 25 illegal immigrants. Their paperwork doesn’t check out, most of them don’t have paperwork at all, so they are completely illegal in the country.

Voice
This man, who’s asked us to withhold his identity, is a team leader from Brave to Love.

Upsound Teamleader
Some of them do have paperwork but we want to check it because we believe that’s some of the manufactured passports that we are after.

Voice
But where is the man behind the fake paperwork?  Chonchobe hasn’t been found, and may have slipped the dragnet earlier that morning. 

ACT 2
Upsound Police
The sooner we can finish up with the paperwork and get them into court, especially the ladies with the kids, the sooner we can finalise the operation.

Voice
Then, an update from the informant. It seems Chonchobe might be in hiding nearby. 

Upsound Teamleader
Team Leader: Our main person of interest, he also rents another room at a secondary location, we are going to go see if he’s there.

Voice
After a short drive, police swoop on these rooms.  
 
But one man refuses to cooperate. 

Upsound Find Ezara
Police: You can come out so long.

Ezara: I just want to take my phone boss.

Police: What’s wrong with you, what’s wrong with you?

Ezara: Nothing.

Police: Sit down.

Voice
After a dramatic morning not short on frustration, Chonchobe is finally in custody.

Upsound Police
We are going to detain you, we are not arresting you, we are going to detain you.

Voice
Police search his room - and find what they’re looking for.

Upsound Team Leader
So these are passports that he bought, so he’s going to take these and modify these and sell it on to his clients.

Voice
Allegedly, Chonchobe buys these real passports for about R200 each and then alters them to reflect the photos and details of his clients. 

Upsound Team Leader
Team Leader: So he pays R200 for this, and then he’s selling it on, well what we heard on the streets is about R4000 for a passport.

Mac: R4000?

Team Leader: R200 you know, for asylum papers.

Voice
Authorities also find allegedly fraudulent visas and asylum seeker permits. They seize this ledger and others showing how lucrative this illicit business is. 

Upsound Mac
So look what we found, this is almost like a register of all the people that have gotten into the country illegally. These guys are running a full on operation here, I mean the guy that they caught says he did about 30 of these just yesterday.


Act 3
Voice
In total, 45 people were detained and arrested during the operation. 39 of them are undocumented foreign nationals now charged with contravening the immigration act.  
 
Ezara Conchobe has been criminally charged with fraud and the manufacturing of fraudulent Department of Home Affairs documents. But this may just be the tip of the iceberg and detectives have been assigned to investigate the extent of the syndicate. 
 
There are no signs of human trafficking having taken place, but Emma van der Walt says it’s a sobering reminder of a much bigger problem. 

Upsound Emma van der Walt
The word is spreading into these countries, like Malawi and Zimbabwe, that they can just come over the border. So it makes the invitation you know, so much more appealing for these people to come into the country. Because they do, they get documentation here.

Voice
Documentation that allows would be criminals all the opportunities in the world to continue a life of crime.



PROMOS

PROMOS
PROMO1
 
VO
We join police on the hunt for a syndicate forging travel documents like passports and visas.
 
Upsound police kicking door
Get down, get down! Down, down, on your knees!
 
VO
And find one of the reasons illegal immigrants are able to cross our borders so easily.

Upsound Team Leader
Then he takes these, and he modifies them, and then he sells them on.


 
 
 
 


PROMO2

Upsound
Sirens and police cars
 
Voice
Exclusive access to a pre-dawn raid where police are on the hunt for a syndicate manufacturing forged travel documents.
 
Upsound Police Search

Voice
But will they find their main suspect?

Up Sound Team Leader
And then he’s selling it on, well what we heard on the streets, for about R4000.

 
PROMO3
 
VO
What do a mysterious plot outside Pretoria, forged travel documents and a surprised ostrich have in common?

Emma
I mean the world’s your oyster, where do you want to go, which passport do you want?

Voice
They’re all part of a major police operation targeting a syndicate forging travel documents.

Upsound Team Leader
Then he takes these, and he modifies them, and then he sells them on.
